Raipur Jail in Chhattisgarh has transformed from a place of incarceration into a rehabilitation centre by launching an initiative to empower women inmates through pickle-making. Female prisoners receive training in producing a variety of pickles, which are sold at the jail canteen and have attracted praise from visitors for their taste. The jail administration aims to provide inmates with practical skills that can support their livelihoods after release. He highlighted a government Memorandum of Understanding with a bank that offers loans to women upon release, facilitating the establishment of pickle-making or food processing businesses and supporting their financial independence. This initiative represents more than a food product; it marks the start of a new life for the women inmates. ranked_evidence.title: FAO Director Yang calls on Agriculture Minister Chaudhary - The Rising Nepal
ranked_evidence.snippet: Kathmandu, July 21: Director of the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)'s South-South and Triangular Cooperation Division, Hua Yang, paid a courtesy call on Minister for Agriculture, Forests and Environment, Gita Chaudhary today. In the meeting that took place at the Ministry in Singha Durbar, they discussed food security, agricultural transformation, sustainable agriculture–food systems, development, and expanding South–South and triangular cooperation in Nepal. On the occasion, Minister Chaudhary said that Nepal is willing to further expand cooperation for transforming the agriculture sector, strengthening food security, and mobilizing international financial resources to that end. The ministry stated that during the meeting, discussions were held on cross-border animal disease control, climate-resilient agricultural development, enhancing the capacity of agricultural laboratories and establishing accredited labs, promoting the export of high-value agricultural products, and strengthening the legal and institutional arrangements related to geographical indications. Minister Chaudhary and the FAO Director on the occasion also expressed a commitment to further strengthening partnerships for sustainable, resilient, and inclusive agricultural and food system development.

ranked_evidence.title: After a bear mauled him, Sitesh Ranjan Deb became a rescuer of Bangladesh’s wildlife - Butler Nature
ranked_evidence.snippet: # After a bear mauled him, Sitesh Ranjan Deb became a rescuer of Bangladesh’s wildlife. * Post author    By Rhett Ayers Butler. The bear came out of the forest with enough force to kill him. During three months in a hospital, he began asking why he was hunting and killing animals. His father and grandfather were known around Sreemangal, in northeastern Bangladesh, for killing leopards, wild boars, and other animals that threatened people or crops. As a boy, Sitesh Ranjan Deb accompanied his father into the forest. The grounds of his home became a treatment center and eventually developed into the Bangladesh Wildlife Service Foundation. When a call came, he collected the animal, found room for it at home, obtained the food it needed, and worked toward the day when its cage could be carried back to the forest and opened. **Sitesh Ranjan Deb turned a hunter’s knowledge to saving wildlife**.

ranked_evidence.title: Legal logging and soaring saplings: the ‘green islands’ bucking the deforestation trend in central America - The Guardian
ranked_evidence.snippet: In Guatemala’s Maya biosphere reserve local people are making a living from trees at the same time as increasing forest cover, showing nature is best protected by those who depend on it. This is sustainable forestry at its most brutal, yet in a few weeks’ time silence will return to this pocket of tropical forest in Guatemala’s Maya biosphere reserve (MBR). Nature will be left to reclaim the land and chainsaws won’t return for at least four years, as part of a strict management plan that is helping to buck the trend of rampant deforestation. The MBR is divided into three zones: a buffer (23%) protects the forest from encroachment around its southern edge, while the rest is divided between a core (39%), which is the base for national parks and conservation areas, and a multiple-use zone (38%), where people are allowed to make a living from the forest – as long as it is done sustainably.

ranked_evidence.title: PM urges eco-friendly brick production to curb air pollution - Bangladesh Post
ranked_evidence.snippet: # PM urges eco-friendly brick production to curb air pollution. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Saturday directed authorities to promote environmentally friendly brick production technologies as part of a broader drive to curb air pollution and improve environmental management. He issued the directive while chairing a meeting on environmental pollution at his Tejgaon office in Dhaka, Prime Minister's Assistant Press Secretary Gazi Shahriar Pamy said. The meeting reviewed a series of measures to tackle air and noise pollution, with particular focus on emissions from brick kilns, one of the country's major sources of air pollution. The Prime Minister stressed the need to accelerate the adoption of alternative, environment-friendly technologies in brick manufacturing to reduce pollution and improve air quality. The meeting also discussed measures to curb excessive use of vehicle horns in the capital. He also instructed the relevant agencies to install automatic traffic signal systems at at least 50 additional intersections across the capital as soon as possible to improve traffic management and reduce congestion.
